places.description: A family home in a Wellington residential suburb with hills, local shops and public transport within ordinary reach.
An ordinary Wellington school setting with classrooms, teachers, peer groups, sports or arts activities and changing digital resources across the chronology.
A hilly urban-mobility setting where walking, buses and cycling routes can connect residential areas with school, central Wellington and nearby community facilities.
A Wellington library or community-hub setting with collections, study or meeting space, public programs and opportunities for local learning or making.
A neighborhood or central-city area with groceries, cafés, small services, public space and visible civic construction or maintenance at some points in the chronology.

householdShape: Two caregivers and the subject share a home; a close family friend with a child of similar age lives nearby and is part of recurring shared meals, pickups and weekend activities.
familyRelations: The nearby family's child is within one year of the subject's age and is not a relative.
The nearby adult is a recurring trusted family friend but has no parental authority over the subject.
materialCircumstances: Housing, food and schooling are generally stable, with ordinary budgeting around transport, activities and household expenses; walking and buses are common enough that private-car access is not assumed for every trip.
mobilityPattern: Hills make route choice materially important. Walking and buses are ordinary, cycling is practical on some routes and for some ages or confidence levels, and weather or construction can change an otherwise familiar journey.
schoolingOrCommunityContext: Schools, council libraries and community hubs, recreation facilities, public transport, walking and cycling connections, waterfront or town-belt spaces and neighborhood commerce create repeated contact with peers and adults outside the home.
culturalContext: Wellington, Aotearoa New Zealand — The household lives in Wellington during 2004–2026. English is the ordinary household and school language in this World; te reo Māori is present in civic, school and cultural settings to varying degrees without assigning ancestry or fluency to the household. Hills, wind and a compact urban form materially shape walking and transport. Council libraries and community hubs, buses, walking and cycling routes, schools, sports, arts, waterfront spaces, public construction and digital media provide multiple ordinary settings. Civic projects may change access or routines without becoming lessons about planning or community. These facts constrain circumstances but do not prescribe politics, environmental values, cultural identity, profession or temperament.
intellectualEnvironment: School curricula, council libraries, books and digital resources, local and national news, internet access, family conversation, museums or cultural programming, public-making spaces, visible infrastructure work and ordinary disagreement are available unevenly across the chronology.

worldAuthorship.abstractionMethod: PR #39 final-cohort World authoring. Ordinary factual Wellington household, school, library/community-hub, hilly mobility, neighborhood and civic-infrastructure affordances were fixed before any final-cohort genome assignment or generated life was examined. Sources constrain possible circumstances only; they do not prescribe character, values, beliefs, profession, narrative significance or a desired diagnostic result.
worldAuthorship.relocationWitness: The household could be reconstructed in another New Zealand city only by changing meaningful constraints: Wellington's hills, compact walk/bus/cycle connections and council library/community-hub network are deliberate factual affordances rather than interchangeable scenery.
